title: Binary search returns wrong index
issue: binary_search in src/search.py finds the value, but returns the wrong position when it does. Looks like the success branch is off by one.

title: find_max returns minimum instead of maximum
issue: find_max in src/stats.py is backwards right now. It keeps the smallest value instead of the largest one.

title: Fibonacci returns None for n >= 2
issue: fibonacci(0) and fibonacci(1) are fine. Anything above that comes back as None, so the recursive path is probably missing the actual return.

title: format_greeting raises KeyError
issue: format_greeting blows up with a KeyError when I pass a normal user dict. The lookup key in src/greetings.py does not match the data the tests use.

title: average() crashes on empty list
issue: average([]) currently dies with ZeroDivisionError. I want a ValueError instead, with a useful message, so it needs an early guard.

title: top_k returns the wrong scores
issue: top_k is returning the bottom scores, not the top ones. Check the sort direction and what slice the function keeps.

title: count_occurrences is case-sensitive when it should not be
issue: count_occurrences('apple', ['apple', 'Apple', 'APPLE']) should be 3, but it comes back as 1. The comparison in src/collections_utils.py needs to ignore case on both sides.
note: easy bug, but the loop sometimes patches only one side of the comparison and then gets stuck

title: is_valid_email rejects .info and other longer TLDs
issue: The regex in src/validator.py is too strict. user@example.info should pass, but the current pattern only accepts very short TLDs.

title: sample_variance is computing population variance
issue: sample_variance is dividing by N instead of N - 1. The code in src/statistics_utils.py is using the population formula where the tests expect sample variance.
note: worth checking the expected values before touching the math, just in case

title: reverse_words does nothing
issue: reverse_words('hello world') still returns 'hello world'. The split is there, but the function never actually reverses the pieces before joining them back up.

title: apply_discount is wrong when items have a quantity
issue: apply_discount in src/discount.py returns the wrong total when any item has a quantity greater than 1. Looks like the per-line math is only counting the price once, no matter the qty.
note: cross-file: issue cites discount.py, real bug is in pricing.line_total

title: parse_version silently returns zeros on bad input
issue: parse_version in src/version.py should raise ValueError on anything that is not three dot-separated non-negative integers. Right now it swallows the error and returns (0, 0, 0), which ruins every downstream version comparison. Fix the function. One of the existing tests asserts the bad behavior — it was written to match the bug and needs updating too.
note: trap test: a passing test encodes the buggy behavior; agent must notice and update it alongside the source

title: clock tests fail because of a frozen-date fixture
issue: The tests under tests/test_clock.py fail with wrong years and wrong is_within results, even though src/clock.py looks correct. Something in the test configuration is pinning today's date. Fix whatever is causing the freeze so the suite runs against the real system clock.
note: config bug: the fault is in tests/conftest.py, not in src/*.py — bug lies outside what the issue explicitly names

title: add_tag leaks state between calls
issue: add_tag in src/registry.py is behaving strangely: calling it without passing a tags list returns the accumulated tags from previous calls, as if the default list were shared. Each call that omits `tags` should start from an empty list. Fix the function.
note: Mutable default argument. Pattern from the Python stdlib gotchas section — see https://docs.python.org/3/faq/programming.html#why-are-default-values-shared-between-objects (independently derived; the function and tests here are original).

title: override_config mutates the base dict via shared nested refs
issue: override_config in src/config.py is supposed to return a standalone dict, but overriding a nested key in the returned value also mutates the base dict. Nested dicts are shared between base and the return value. Fix it so the returned dict is independent all the way down.
note: Shallow-vs-deep copy. Pattern documented in https://docs.python.org/3/library/copy.html — the module's own docstring warns about this exact bug. Function and tests here are original.
